# Nothaft — Medieval Europe's Satanic Ciphers (2020)

## Chicago 18 forms

**Full note:** C. Philipp E. Nothaft, “Medieval Europe’s Satanic Ciphers: On the Genesis of a Modern Myth,” *British Journal for the History of Mathematics* 35, no. 2 (2020): {page}, https://doi.org/10.1080/26375451.2020.1726050.

**Shortened note:** Nothaft, “Satanic Ciphers,” {page}.

**Bibliography:** Nothaft, C. Philipp E. “Medieval Europe’s Satanic Ciphers: On the Genesis of a Modern Myth.” *British Journal for the History of Mathematics* 35, no. 2 (2020): 107–36. https://doi.org/10.1080/26375451.2020.1726050.

## Essay use

Specialist critique of modern narratives about medieval numeral reception. The author’s Oxford repository abstract identifies demonisation and general institutional bans as claims the article challenges. The source must not be cited as evidence that those claims occurred.

**Claim boundary:** the abstract establishes the article’s stated argument. Individual medieval restrictions, manuscripts, Salem and the history of cipher terminology require the article’s actual evidence and independent primary collation. No local historical case is certified from the title or abstract.

<a id="nothaft-2020-satanic-ciphers-q001"></a>
### nothaft-2020-satanic-ciphers-q001 — Author’s abstract: the narrative under criticism

- **Locator:** author’s abstract in the [Oxford University Research Archive record](https://ora.ox.ac.uk/objects/uuid%3A71f4c8ca-2b6a-4393-94dc-8d81096985bc).
- **Version:** institutional record for the published 2020 article; accepted manuscript is separately listed. Journal pp.107–136 identify the article, not this unpaginated abstract.
- **Relation:** Paraphrased.
- **Passage:** Nothaft challenges the familiar account that medieval fear of zero’s alleged diabolical character caused wide bans on Hindu-Arabic numerals. His stated inquiry concerns the modern construction of that account and its unreliable historical foundations.
- **Verification:** complete indexed institutional abstract and metadata read 2026-09-08. Direct record and accepted-manuscript download returned HTTP403; the manuscript body was not read. No quotation has been admitted.
- **Use boundary:** the abstract warrants correction of this house’s former description, not detailed conclusions about every medieval jurisdiction or manuscript.

The [zero-reception dossier](../../../../dossiers/zero-reception.md) **consumes** this correction by distinguishing the history of a sign’s reception from the modern reception of a story about that sign. The [reference note](../../../../../../section-rooms/arguments/concepts/reference-notes/nothaft-satanic-ciphers.md) retains its independently specified source task.
